sentence: This project studies how proteins that bind RNA and a transcription factor work together to control the fate of stem cells during quiescence.
This project tries to prevent type 1 diabetes in people at risk and to learn more about its risk factors.
This project studies how tandem repeat expansions in the human genome contribute to Alzheimer’s disease.
This project runs clinical trials to improve the health of children and adults with neurological disease.
This project builds computer methods that combine molecular networks to find large-scale disease pathways.
This project builds polymer brush coated cell culture substrates to study how ligand patterns shape macrophage polarization.
This project studies how epigenetic regulation of trained immunity affects thoracic aortic aneurysms and dissections.
This project tries to find out how a signaling node between tumor cells and the brain environment promotes breast cancer brain metastases.
This project combines biostatistics and epidemiology methods to support research on HIV and AIDS.
This project studies how traumatic brain injury changes neuronal assemblies underlying cognition, using electrophysiology measures and behavioral tasks.
This project tests how specific bacteria promote the growth of tumor cells in a precursor state to multiple myeloma.
This project studies how metabolism changes in mitochondrial disease by measuring metabolic fluxes in animals and humans.
This project prepares samples and coordinates genome wide analyses to study how early life stress raises cardiovascular disease risk.
This project tries to understand how melanocytes and keratinocytes interact in normal states and in basal cell carcinoma.
This project looks for cardiometabolic biomarkers and builds bioelectronic devices for early detection, focusing on brain health.
This project uses statistical methods to study how alcohol use and social determinants relate to health outcomes among people with HIV.
This project uses network models to find processes in the host immune response that predict how severe COVID-19 becomes.
This project supports research into the causes of neurodevelopmental disorders and works to develop therapies for them.
This project studies how DNA in extracellular vesicles from Candida albicans activates an innate immune pathway.
This project studies epigenetic signs in cell-free DNA from blood plasma of people who were later diagnosed with cancer.
